nodes.label: desktop memory - memory is downstream of conversation

Frozen copy taken 2026-08-03 of the desktop machine's memory file - the live directory sits on the other machine and is not reachable from here, so this copy is what there is to review. Listed unreviewed in REVIEW_REGISTER.md section 6. Memory is a downstream snapshot of what the user said at some past point, and the live conversation is the source of truth: if something he says now conflicts with a memory, the conversation wins and the memory needs updating, not the other way around. He is iterating on a design and his thinking moves, so a memory written two days ago reflects two-days-ago thinking - load-bearing then, possibly stale now - and treating memory as authoritative over the live conversation flips the directionality and produces stale or wrong work. His words: 'the data flows from here to the files.' When he contradicts a memory in conversation, do not argue with him from the memory - update it; when recalling a memory before acting, treat it as what was true when it was written and verify it is still true if the action depends on it; do not quote memory back to him as the reason for doing or not doing something; and when the conversation establishes a new fact or decision that supersedes a memory, update the memory in the same turn, not later. CANON_AUDIT.md lists this among the grounded, verbatim-quoted and correct desktop entries
